ai.description: This small snake reaches 60 cm. It is pale brown with black-edged crossbands and a distinct chevron mark on the head. It features a specialized, blade-like tooth for slicing reptile eggs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Oligodon arnensis* is the presence of distinct, dark-edged black cross-bands across its body, paired with a prominent chevron-shaped mark on the nape of its head.
ai.habitat: The Common Kukri Snake inhabits diverse environments, ranging from dry deciduous forests and scrublands to agricultural fields and gardens, typically below 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Common Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slit open reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Common Kukri Snake is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs from March to August, with eggs often deposited in termite mounds.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Common Kukri Snake is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to southern India, typically below 2,000 meters.
